ei.title: Why Cramming Fails as a Learning Strategy
ei.subject: 9월_2024 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Why Cramming Fails as a Learning Strategy

fullPassage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. Focusing on exploring new topics rather than reviewing the same material over and over again can improve your academic performance. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.

questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an (A)[active / passive] form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts (B)[strengthening / disappearing], and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. Focusing on exploring new topics rather than reviewing the same material over and over again can improve your academic performance. To get information into long-term memory, it is (C)[optional / essential] to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
(A) active(활동적인) ↔ passive(수동적인): 정보는 의식적 작업 기억에 '활동적인' 형태로 존재
(B) disappearing(사라지는) ↔ strengthening(강화되는): 작업 기억은 곧 '사라지기' 시작
(C) essential(필수적인) ↔ optional(선택적인): 장기 기억을 위해 공부와 시험이 '필수적'
따라서 active - disappearing - essential

questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our (A)[conscious / unconscious] working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes (B)[minimal / enormous]: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. Focusing on exploring new topics rather than reviewing the same material over and over again can (C)[reduce / improve] your academic performance. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
(A) conscious(의식적인) ↔ unconscious(무의식적인): 정보는 '의식적인' 작업 기억에 존재
(B) enormous(엄청난) ↔ minimal(아주 적은): 며칠 뒤 소실 효과가 '엄청나게' 커짐
(C) improve(향상시키다) ↔ reduce(줄이다): 학업 성취를 '향상시킨다'는 문맥
따라서 conscious - enormous - improve

questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to (A)[differentiate / combine] between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to (B)[forget / recall] the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. Focusing on (C)[avoiding / exploring] new topics rather than reviewing the same material over and over again can improve your academic performance. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
(A) differentiate(구별하다) ↔ combine(결합하다): 기억의 여러 부분을 '구별하지' 못함
(B) recall(떠올리다) ↔ forget(잊다): 며칠 뒤 같은 정보를 '떠올리기' 위해 장기 기억 필요
(C) exploring(탐구하는 것) ↔ avoiding(피하는 것): 새로운 주제를 '탐구하는' 것
따라서 differentiate - recall - exploring

questions.passage: Why do we have the ①<u>illusion</u> that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to ②<u>differentiate</u> between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes ③<u>minimal</u>: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. Focusing on exploring new topics rather than reviewing the same material over and over again can improve your academic performance. To get information into long-term memory, it is ④<u>essential</u> to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① illusion(착각) — 벼락치기가 최선이라는 '착각'. 적절
❌ ② differentiate(구별하다) — 기억의 부분을 '구별'하지 못함. 적절
✅ ③ minimal(아주 적은) — 원문은 enormous(엄청난). 며칠 뒤 효과가 커지는 맥락에서 반대 ←정답
❌ ④ essential(필수적인) — 공부와 시험이 '필수적'. 적절

questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you ③<u>retest</u> your knowledge, memory vanishes. Focusing on exploring new topics rather than reviewing the same material over and over again can ④<u>improve</u> your academic performance. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① unconscious(무의식적인) — 원문은 conscious(의식적인). 활동적 작업 기억은 '의식적'이어야 하므로 반대 ←정답
❌ ② recall(떠올리다) — 같은 정보를 '떠올림'. 적절
❌ ③ retest(다시 시험하다) — 지식을 '다시 시험'. 적절
❌ ④ improve(향상시키다) — 학업 성취를 '향상'. 적절

To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① differentiate(구별하다) — 기억의 부분을 '구별'하지 못함. 적절

questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is __________? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. Focusing on exploring new topics rather than reviewing the same material over and over again can improve your academic performance. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
